concepts: A monsoon-palace princess is forced to marry a brooding rakshasa king to save her drowning kingdom.
A human bride is promised to a naga prince in a vague mythic serpent kingdom; they turn out to be fated mates.
A courtesan spy in a Mughal-style court falls for the crown prince she was sent to ruin.
A spice-and-silk merchant princess clashes with a pirate captain on a pepper coast.
An apsara exiled from heaven falls for the mortal warrior she was sent to tempt.
Fated mates from rival sun and moon dynasties in an unnamed mythic India.
A princess's swayamvara becomes a deadly tournament, and she falls for the outsider champion.
A temple dancer falls for the assassin sent to kill her.
Lovers reincarnated across the ages, cursed by a god, meet again.
A demon king keeps a captive bride in his jungle fortress and she tames him.
titles: A Court of Monsoon and Marigold

concepts.title: Vow of Teeth
concepts.hook_line: A shapeshifting assassin must kill the lord she was married off to, but he's the one man who has seen her night-shape, and whoever names it can trap her in it forever.
concepts.premise: Neela is an odiyan, a guild assassin who becomes a leopard at night, married into the household of the hill-fort warden she has been paid to kill. On the wedding night he wakes to see her change, and keeps his mouth shut. Now the man she must murder holds the one word that could cage her for life, and he is using his silence to bargain for the name of whoever bought his death.
comps: The Serpent and the Wings of Night
concepts.folklore: Odiyan shapeshifting assassins, Malabar (north Kerala hill country), with kalari fighting and marma strikes as texture
concepts.world_rule: An odiyan changes shape at night with a guild resin. Her night-shape is a secret: anyone who witnesses her change and speaks what she is aloud before dawn locks her in that shape forever. The guild masters hold every member's witnessed name in a ledger, and that is their leash. Being seen is the intimate act that costs.
concepts.heat: Open door, moderate: 2 to 3 explicit scenes per book, each changing the bargain between them
concepts.darkness: Dark edges: contract killing, a guild that owns its members, the death of Neela's guild-sister in book 1 that stays lost; no sexual violence

leads.heroine: Neela, 27, odiyan assassin and contract bride
leads.love_interest: Devan, 32, warden of the hill fort Kettamala and the queen's border commander

first_look.who_falls_for_whom: A bride-assassin and the husband she's paid to kill
first_look.danger: She must murder him; he can cage her with one word
first_look.twist: Being seen changing is what gives a lover power over her, so every night together is a test of whether he'll speak

concepts.cover_concept: A woman's hand in a gold wedding bangle lies flat on a man's bare chest, the nails turning to leopard claws, against black and turmeric-gold.

originality.note: Without the witnessed-shape rule his silence is worthless; the romance is built on a power he declines to use.
Is safety worth being unseen? Neela's guild says yes and has kept her alive; Devan says no and could get her caged.
Devan wants to find who in the queen's council is selling the border, a goal that predates his marriage.
The guild is a system and a ledger. Killing its master just hands the ledger to the next holder.
Neela believes being known is being owned; she ends book 1 by choosing to change in front of him.
Inverted: she is the deadly one and he holds power through restraint. Honoured: the arranged-marriage slow burn ending in a real marriage.
'An assassin bride who turns into a leopard, and the husband who has seen her and won't say it.'
Witnessing a change is a political key: the guild runs on it, and a husband who holds it can break the guild's monopoly.

concepts.title: The Oracle Cannot Lie
concepts.hook_line: A mountain oracle who cannot lie must win her god's case at the great gathering, but her rival speaks for the enemy god, and loving him would silence hers.
concepts.premise: Every valley's god rules through a human oracle who can never speak a lie, and at the winter gathering the gods argue their valleys' disputes through them. Tara must win back the stream the next valley has dammed, or her village dies by summer. Her opponent is Vikram, the rival god's oracle and an ex-soldier who protects her from the assassins circling the gathering, and a god leaves any oracle who takes a lover.
concepts.folklore: Devta courts, oracles and the procession of gods to a great gathering, Himachal (Kullu and Mandi valley inspired), with invented devtas
concepts.world_rule: An oracle cannot speak a lie, possessed or not. Gods vote at the gathering through their oracles. A god withdraws from an oracle who takes a lover, and the valley loses its voice and protection. Any direct question about her heart is a danger, so the intimate act that costs is being asked.
concepts.heat: Open door, moderate: 2 to 3 explicit scenes per book, none during possession, each forcing a political consequence
concepts.darkness: Dark edges: drought and a dying village, assassination at the gathering, a forged god; Tara's office is lost for good

leads.heroine: Tara, 30, oracle of the Grey Ram, god of Sarol valley
leads.love_interest: Vikram, 34, oracle of the Snow-Eyed Lady of Dhura valley, former mercenary captain

first_look.who_falls_for_whom: Two rival oracles arguing opposite sides of a life-or-death case
first_look.danger: Their gods are enemies, and a lover costs an oracle her god
first_look.twist: Neither can lie, so the forbidden romance can't be hidden; one honest question exposes them

concepts.cover_concept: Two silver ritual masks, one ram-horned and one snow-white, face each other nose to nose over a snowy mountain ridge, their breath mingling.

originality.note: Without the no-lie rule they could hide the affair; the romance is defined by being unable to deny it.
Who gets the water when both valleys need it? Both oracles have a legitimate case.
Vikram wants to find out who poisoned his predecessor at the last gathering.
The conflict is a water dispute between two valleys that both need the stream; no villain's death fixes it.
Tara believes justice has one right answer and the god knows it; she ends by co-authoring a shared answer.
Inverted: forbidden love without secrets, because neither can lie. Honoured: rivals to lovers with high-stakes sparring.
'Two oracles who can't lie, on opposite sides of a trial of gods, falling for each other.'
A kiss strips a valley of its vote; love is literally a political act.

concepts.title: The Iron Nail
concepts.hook_line: A bound night-spirit must win her freedom from the man who holds her iron nail, but every kiss feeds her on his life, and freeing her unleashes her hunger.
concepts.premise: Eighty years ago Malli was murdered and became a yakshi, a night-spirit of the pala tree, and the head of the house that wronged her drove an iron nail through her into its trunk. His grandson Kiran inherits the nail, the debts and the creditors, and wakes her as the only weapon he has left. She can feed only on her keeper, every touch costs him a season of life, and she wants to be free of the family that killed her.
concepts.folklore: Yakshi spirits of the pala tree and binding by iron nail, with tharavad matriliny, central Kerala lagoon country (Kuttanad inspired)
concepts.world_rule: A yakshi bound by an iron nail wakes only for whoever holds the nail and can feed only on that keeper. Each feeding by breath or blood costs the keeper a season of life. Pull the nail and she is free, but free to feed on anyone. Touch is the intimate act that costs.
concepts.heat: Open door, moderate: 2 to 3 explicit scenes per book, the first only after Kiran gives her the nail and she chooses freely
concepts.darkness: Gothic: inherited murder, a house built on a crime, years of Kiran's life spent for good; no sexual violence, and her past death is never eroticised

leads.heroine: Malli, yakshi, died at 26 and adult in mind and body, bound for eighty years
leads.love_interest: Kiran, 34, eldest man and keeper of a debt-ruined tharavad, guardian of his niece's inheritance

first_look.who_falls_for_whom: A bound night-spirit and the man who holds her chain
first_look.danger: Loving him eats his life; freeing her endangers everyone
first_look.twist: He is the grandson of the man who killed her, and the only person she can feed on

concepts.cover_concept: A single rusted iron nail driven through a white pala blossom, a red-bordered sari trailing into black lagoon water below.

originality.note: Without the nail and the keeper-only feeding there is no captivity and no cost to touch; the romance is the rule.
Do we owe repair for crimes we didn't commit? Kiran's creditors and Malli's grief give two legitimate answers.
Kiran must keep his niece's inherited land out of a creditor-lord's hands.
The killer is long dead; the wrong lives in the house's title deeds and in the nail.
Malli believes no one of that house can be anything but her jailer; she ends by choosing to return to the house as its guardian.
Inverted: the monster is the heroine and the man is the jailer who must repair. Honoured: monster romance where she is desired unchanged, hunger and all.
'A murdered spirit nailed to a tree, and the killer's grandson who has to choose whether to free her.'
Whoever holds the nail holds a weapon in a land dispute; their intimacy decides who owns the house.

concepts.title: Bound till the Thaw
concepts.hook_line: A smuggler must guide the warden sworn to hang her over a closed winter pass, but the mountain spirits bind them till the thaw, and every lie to him freezes her.
concepts.premise: Meera runs medicine and salt over the high pass after it closes, and Captain Rohan has spent three winters hunting her crew. When an avalanche traps them on the same side of the pass, with a fever spreading in the valley beyond and the queen's seal in his coat, the mountain spirits let them cross only if they are rope-bound. Bound till the thaw, they cannot walk out of each other's reach, and the cold takes its toll from every lie.
comps: A Court of Thorns and Roses
concepts.folklore: Jogini mountain spirits of the high passes and winter pass closure, Himachal (Kinnaur and upper Sutlej trade route inspired)
concepts.world_rule: In winter the high-pass spirits let only rope-bound pairs cross. A bound pair can't separate beyond a rope's length until the first thaw. Each lie told to your bound partner costs body heat in proportion to its size, and a great lie can kill. Promises and confessions are the intimate acts that cost.
concepts.heat: Open door, moderate: 2 to 3 explicit scenes per book, each tied to a truth that changes the bond
concepts.darkness: Survival darkness: frostbite, avalanche, a fever village; Meera loses two fingers to a lie she chose to tell; no sexual violence

leads.heroine: Meera, 29, smuggler-guide of the high pass
leads.love_interest: Rohan, 35, captain of the queen's pass-wardens

first_look.who_falls_for_whom: A smuggler and the warden hunting her
first_look.danger: He's sworn to hang her crew; the mountain can kill either of them
first_look.twist: Every lie to him freezes her, so the enemies have to be truthful

concepts.cover_concept: Two gloved hands bound wrist to wrist by a red wool rope, dusted in snow, against a jagged blue-white ridge.

originality.note: Remove the lie-cold rule and the rope and this becomes a plain road trip; the bond forces honesty and proximity.
Is the law worth more than the lives it fails? Rohan's border law and Meera's smuggling both save people.
Rohan must deliver the queen's seal before a regent's coup in the far valley.
The enemy is winter, a border law and a fever; there is no villain to kill.
Meera believes the law is only ever a noose; she ends by helping Rohan write a winter-crossing law.
Inverted: the heroine is the expert and leader, the soldier the dependent. Honoured: forced proximity with one fire and a slow burn.
'A smuggler and a lawman roped together over a winter pass where lying freezes you.'
A confession across the rope can convict her crew or clear them; truth between lovers is evidence.
